findings.claim: Dead-letter requeue is not atomic with its state check and can fail or produce an inconsistent result when purge runs concurrently.
findings.evidence: Lines 68-74 perform an unlocked read/check; lines 76-83 issue independent writes; lines 84-85 assume the row still exists. storage.purge_terminal deletes DONE/DEAD rows without coordinating with this sequence (storage.py:240-245).
findings.root_cause: The method reads the task, checks DEAD, then performs reset_attempts and mark_state as separate autocommit statements without a write transaction or conditional UPDATE. purge_terminal can delete the row between these operations; the subsequent get returns None and triggers an AssertionError. Concurrent administrative operations therefore turn a valid requeue request into a server error.
findings.suggested_verification: Run requeue and purge concurrently against the same DEAD task, or inject a delete between the initial get and reset_attempts; observe the assertion/500 response.
